newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends up on lack of selling.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends up on lack of selling.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher amid scale down mill-buying and a lack of producer-related selling, traders said.

"Our cash market will continue to keep the spread trading at an inverse because producers just aren't selling. Mills and exporters are having a real tough time (sourcing wheat)," a MGE floor source said.
Wheat also showed some strength toward the close on KCBT- and CBOT-related buying.
MGE spring wheat closed one to four cents per bushel higher, with December up four cents at $4.22.
Traders said volumes were extremely light Monday.
"It was pathetic -- very easy to move the market one way or the other if you had an order," a trader said.

A players' sheet showed LFG having bought 600,000 Dec bushels. The Dec/March spread traded from 13 to 14-1/2 cents per bushel. Locals and Atwood-Peavey bull-spread Dec/March and Benson Quinn, CIS and Wilson were bear-spreaders.
MGE Dec and March barley futures both closed two cents per cwt lower, with Dec down two at $6.95 per cwt.
